name: One supervisor, three specialists
note: Both runs are real run_supervisor output over scripted router/policies. Expand a handoff to read the worker's inner loop — each worker's context contains ONLY its own ticket.

workers.name: policy_worker
workers.description: Answers policy questions. Read-only access to the policy.

workers.name: refund_worker
workers.description: Handles refund requests end-to-end: order facts, policy check, gated refund write.

workers.name: frontdesk_worker
workers.description: Escalates to a human with a clean handoff summary. No tools.

scenarios.label: Triage day
scenarios.task: Handle the queue: T1 (policy question) · T2 (refund request) · T3 (wants a human)
scenarios.predict: Three tickets, three specialists with different tools. Who gets what — and does any worker ever see another worker's ticket?
scenarios.lesson: Each specialist ran with a clean context (only its own ticket), least-privilege tools, and returned through the supervisor — no worker-to-worker chatter. The supervisor's lane plus the inner traces is the whole debugging story.
scenarios.summary: Queue handled. T1: Per our policy: You may request a refund within 30 days of purchase. Items marked as clearance may be exchanged for store credit instead. | T2: Done! Refund initiated for order 18342. Confirmation R-18342. You'll see the money back on the original payment method within 5 business days. | T3: Escalated to a human agent with full context: Ticket T3: This is the THIRD time I'm writing. I want a human. Now.

scenarios.label: Sick day (failure isolation)
scenarios.task: Same queue — but the refund worker is stuck in Chapter 8's loop
scenarios.predict: The refund specialist will fail (loop guard). Does the whole queue fail with it?
scenarios.lesson: Failure isolation: the worker's loop_detected status became a record the router could read, the ticket was rerouted to the front desk, and the queue still completed — degraded, not dead. One agent's failure should cost one handoff, never the run.
